[Part three](03-tool-use-mcp.qmd) solved "how does an agent call a tool," with
MCP. This post solves a different problem I actually expect to run into soon:
how do two independent agents, built by different teams, in different
frameworks, running on different machines, talk to each other as peers, not as
a tool call. Google's Agent2Agent protocol, A2A, is the answer.

Concretely, in my own setup: my error-analysis agent is raw Python plus
aisuite, but a colleague's synthetic-data agent might end up in LangGraph, and
some future scheduling agent might live inside Google ADK, especially given
where Infineon seems to be looking. Without a shared protocol, wiring those
three together means a custom integration for every single pair. A2A gives all
of them a common language instead.

## Jargon, explained simply

**A2A.** Agent2Agent protocol, an open standard letting independent agents
discover each other's capabilities and delegate tasks, regardless of what
framework built either side.

**Agent Card.** A small JSON document an agent publishes describing what it can
do and how to reach it, the agent equivalent of an API spec.

**Task, in A2A terms.** A unit of work one agent delegates to another, sent as
structured JSON, with the receiving agent able to report progress and return a
result.

**Signed Agent Card.** A cryptographically signed version of the card, so a
receiving agent can verify it actually came from the domain it claims to.

**Skill, in A2A terms.** One specific capability an agent exposes, listed
inside its Agent Card, with defined input and output formats.

## MCP versus A2A, in one sentence

MCP is agent to tool. A2A is agent to agent. They solve different layers of
the same overall problem, and I use both, not one instead of the other.

## Publishing my error-analysis agent as an A2A agent

Here's a real Agent Card for the error-analysis agent from [part
five](05-planning-multiagent.qmd), so any other A2A-compatible agent can
discover and call it.

Install the reference SDK with `pip install a2a-sdk`.

Save this as `agent_card.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "semiconductor-error-analysis-agent",
  "description": "Reviews segmentation pipeline verdicts and decides whether a case needs human review.",
  "url": "https://internal.example.com/a2a/error-analysis",
  "capabilities": {
    "streaming": true
  },
  "skills": [
    {
      "id": "review-void-verdict",
      "description": "Given a void-ratio verdict and image metadata, decide if human review is required.",
      "inputModes": ["text/plain", "application/json"],
      "outputModes": ["application/json"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## A minimal A2A server wrapping my existing agent

Here's the server side, exposing the same `error_analysis_agent` function from
part five, using the reference Python SDK.

Save this as `a2a_server.py`:

```python
from a2a.server import A2AServer
from a2a.types import Task, TaskResult
import aisuite as ai

client = ai.Client()

def error_analysis_agent(verdict_text: str) -> str:
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="openai:gpt-4o-mini",
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": "You are an error-analysis agent for a "
             "semiconductor imaging pipeline."},
            {"role": "user", "content": "Given this verdict, decide if it needs "
             "human review and why: " + verdict_text}
        ]
    )
    return response.choices[0].message.content


def handle_task(task: Task) -> TaskResult:
    verdict_text = task.input.get("verdict_text", "")
    decision = error_analysis_agent(verdict_text)
    return TaskResult(output={"decision": decision})


server = A2AServer(agent_card_path="agent_card.json", task_handler=handle_task)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    server.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=9000)
```

Any A2A-compatible client, regardless of what framework built it, LangGraph,
CrewAI, ADK, or raw Python like mine, can fetch `agent_card.json`, see that I
expose a `review-void-verdict` skill, and send a task without either side
needing to know anything about the other's internals.

## Calling another team's A2A agent from my own pipeline

Here's the client side: my linear pipeline from part five, delegating the
final review step to a remote A2A agent instead of a local Python function.

```python
from a2a.client import A2AClient

a2a_client = A2AClient()

def remote_error_analysis(verdict_text: str) -> str:
    card = a2a_client.fetch_agent_card("https://internal.example.com/a2a/error-analysis")
    task = a2a_client.create_task(
        agent_card=card,
        skill_id="review-void-verdict",
        input={"verdict_text": verdict_text},
    )
    result = a2a_client.wait_for_result(task)
    return result.output["decision"]
```

This function is a drop-in replacement for the local `error_analysis_agent`
call in my part-five pipeline, the rest of the pipeline code doesn't change at
all, only where that one step actually executes.

## When I'd actually reach for this, versus when I wouldn't

If every agent in a system lives in my own codebase, MCP for tools plus plain
Python function calls between my own agents is genuinely enough, I would not
add A2A just because it exists. I'd reach for it specifically when agents cross
an organizational or framework boundary, a vendor's inspection-equipment agent
needing to talk to mine, or a separate team's agent, built in a framework I
don't control, needing to hand off work into my pipeline. That boundary-
crossing case is exactly what A2A was built for, and it's also exactly the
situation I expect to hit once more teams here start building their own
agents.
